title: D6: how the book is ordered, and what each choice changes
headline: D6 is the storyteller's plan draft 6: it brings the signed plan (draft 5) in line with RC1, which grew three new parts this morning at your word (a map chapter, 'what was already there', concepts and principles). Six choices: where each new part goes, chapter 0, the length, and the Cold-Read chapter. One caution first: your voice memo of tonight moves the book's centre of gravity to agentic workflows, as a walkthrough. That may reshape the structure itself, so you may prefer to sign D6 only after the name and structure study it asks for.

sections.title: How your voice memo bears on this
sections.text: D6 keeps the book's current spine: the insider argument, told through the day. Your memo says the book is not about the insider agent (that is a separate book, and the talk needed more rounds), but a pragmatic, example-driven walkthrough of agentic workflows in October 2026: collaboration, a multidisciplinary team kept aligned by shared protocols and open information, and the plumbing (the non-functional requirements) built while making the talk. That is a change of spine, not of order. Two ways to take it: sign D6 now (the order holds either way, and the revision can start), or hold D6 until the name and structure study reports, so the book is restructured once.

for_you.ask: Sign D6 now, or after the name and structure study?
for_you.recommend: Hold D6 until the study: your memo changes what the book is for, and the order should follow from that, not come before it.
